claims.text: A 10% reduction in sodium consumption over 10 years within each country is projected to avert approximately 5.8 million DALYs per year related to cardiovascular diseases worldwide.
A 10% national sodium reduction policy has a population weighted mean cost of I$1.13 per capita over a 10-year intervention period.
The population weighted mean cost effectiveness ratio of a 10% sodium reduction policy over 10 years is approximately I$204 per DALY saved.
Among nine world regions, estimated cost effectiveness of sodium reduction is best in South Asia at I$116 per DALY.
Among the world's 30 most populous countries, the cost effectiveness of sodium reduction is best in Uzbekistan at I$26.08 per DALY.
Among the world's 30 most populous countries, the cost effectiveness of sodium reduction in Myanmar is I$33.30 per DALY.
Cost effectiveness of sodium reduction is lowest in Australia/New Zealand at I$880 per DALY, or 0.02 times GDP per capita.
96.0% of the world's adult population lives in countries where a soft regulation sodium reduction policy has a cost effectiveness ratio under 0.1 times GDP per capita.
99.6% of the world's adult population lives in countries where a soft regulation sodium reduction policy has a cost effectiveness ratio under 1.0 times GDP per capita.

evidence.description: Worldwide, a 10% reduction in sodium consumption over 10 years within each country was projected to avert approximately 5.8 million DALYs/year related to cardiovascular diseases.
At a population weighted mean cost of I$1.13 per capita over the 10 year intervention.
The population weighted mean cost effectiveness ratio was approximately I$204/DALY.
Across nine world regions, estimated cost effectiveness of sodium reduction was best in South Asia (I$116/DALY).
Across the world's 30 most populous countries, best in Uzbekistan (I$26.08/DALY).
Across the world's 30 most populous countries, best in Uzbekistan (I$26.08/DALY) and Myanmar (I$33.30/DALY).
Cost effectiveness was lowest in Australia/New Zealand (I$880/DALY, or 0.02×gross domestic product (GDP) per capita).
Most (96.0%) of the world's adult population lived in countries in which this intervention had a cost effectiveness ratio <0.1×GDP per capita.
And 99.6% in countries with a cost effectiveness ratio <1.0×GDP per capita.

methodologies.name: Global comparative risk assessment and cost-effectiveness modeling
methodologies.description: Global modeling study evaluating country-specific costs using the WHO NCD Costing Tool and impact on mortality and DALYs via comparative risk assessment across 183 nations over 10 years.

limitations.text: The evaluation only modeled program costs without incorporating potential healthcare savings from prevented cardiovascular events.
